core_summary: This chapter explores the biological mechanisms of reproduction across asexual and sexual modes. It emphasizes DNA copying as the foundation of reproduction and source of evolutionary variation. The chapter reviews asexual modes (fission, fragmentation, regeneration, budding, vegetative propagation, spore formation) in single and simpler multicellular organisms. It examines sexual reproduction in flowering plants (pollination, double fertilisation, seed development) and human reproductive anatomy, pubertal changes, fertilization, embryonic development, and contraceptive methods.
key_concepts: Importance of accurate DNA copying and biochemical apparatus creation for species stability and evolutionary variation

Asexual reproduction modes: Binary fission (Amoeba, Leishmania), Multiple fission (Plasmodium), Fragmentation (Spirogyra), Regeneration (Planaria, Hydra), Budding (Hydra, Yeast), Vegetative Propagation (Bryophyllum, cuttings, layering, grafting), and Spore formation (Rhizopus)
Significance of sexual reproduction in combining genetic material from two individuals, utilizing haploid germ-cells generated via meiotic cell division to maintain species chromosome count
Anatomy of flowering plants (angiosperms): Stamens (anther producing pollen grains) and Pistil (stigma, style, ovary containing ovules)
Pollination mechanisms (self vs cross) followed by pollen tube growth, fertilization of female germ-cell inside ovule, zygote formation, and seed/fruit development
Human reproductive systems: Pubertal changes triggered by sex hormones (testosterone, oestrogen)
Male anatomy: Testes in scrotum (sperm production & testosterone), vas deferens, prostate/seminal vesicle secretions, urethra
Female anatomy: Ovaries (egg release), fallopian tubes (site of fertilization), uterus (site of implantation & placenta nourishment), vagina, and menstrual cycle mechanism when unfertilized
Contraceptive strategies: Barrier methods (condoms), Chemical/Hormonal pills, Intrauterine devices (Copper-T), and Surgical procedures (vasectomy, tubectomy) for family planning and STD prevention

key_terms.definition: The cellular process of replicating genetic material prior to cell division, ensuring inheritance with subtle variations.
Mode of reproduction producing offspring from a single parent without the fusion of gametes.
Asexual division of a unicellular organism into two equal daughter cells.
The ability of an organism to regrow complete individual bodies from severed body fragments using specialized stem cells.
Asexual reproduction in plants where new individuals arise from vegetative structures like roots, stems, or leaves.
Mode of reproduction involving the fusion of male and female haploid gametes from two parents.
The transfer of pollen grains from the anther of a stamen to the receptive stigma of a pistil.
The fusion of the male gamete with the female egg cell to form a diploid zygote.
A specialized vascular tissue disc embedded in the uterine wall providing oxygen and nutrients to the embryo and removing wastes.
The monthly shedding of the thickened blood-rich uterine lining when egg fertilization does not occur.
Deliberate methods or devices used to prevent pregnancy during sexual intercourse.

key_takeaways: DNA copying errors generate variations that enhance species resilience against changing ecological niches.
Meiotic cell division reduces chromosome numbers by half in gametes, ensuring diploid restoration upon fertilization.
After fertilization in plants, the ovule develops into a protective seed containing the embryo, while the ovary ripens into a fruit.
Human fertilization occurs within the fallopian tube, followed by blastocyst implantation in the vascularized uterine lining.
Barrier methods like condoms serve dual functions by preventing unintended pregnancy and shielding against sexually transmitted diseases (STDs).
